{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM Hosting Services Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of vendor draft (Base Terms; § 3.1 Term and related provisions)
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney-Client Communication**

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the vendor draft against our playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit and no audit right running against us, and New York law applies. IBM's IP infringement indemnity is uncapped and sits at or above our fallback, IP ownership of deliverables and our data meets the fallback, assignment sits at the fallback, and we hold a one-month convenience termination right with no reciprocal right for IBM.

Seven items require attention. The most significant are (i) the liability regime, which contains no carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud and expressly excludes IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data in a hosting deal; (ii) the Base Components licence, which is expressly revocable at will and limited to us alone with no Affiliate or contractor coverage; and (iii) the renewal mechanic, which auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term on a 90-day non-renewal window. We also have three gaps or shortfalls to close: unquantified early termination charges, the absence of any conformance warranty, and the total absence of transition-assistance, data-return and insurance obligations.

Three findings fall into what our playbook treats as walk-away territory: the revocable, non-extensible licence grant; automatic multi-year renewal; and the absence of any insurance covenant from a vendor hosting our environment and processing personal data on our behalf.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Caps are mutual at 12 months' charges (min. $100,000) with indemnity and bodily injury/property damage outside, but there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records or data. Fails the fallback on carve-outs. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | Defend-and-indemnify IP indemnity (patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret) with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies; uncapped under § 9.1(a). Sits at or above the fallback. Secondary asks only: no indemnity for breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and our reverse indemnity at § 8.2(a)(3) is broadly drafted. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers | We own Type I Materials; IBM retains Type II Materials but grants an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence. No assignment of our Content and no joint ownership — meets the fallback. Secondary asks: Type II licence limited to US Enterprise use, default classification as Type II, breadth of the Type I licence-back, no affirmative statement that we retain Content ownership. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Base Components licence is expressly revocable, limited to us alone (no Affiliates or contractors; § 14.17 confirms no other rights), with no path to add them. Walk-away case under our playbook. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Convenience exit is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges set by Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no cap in the Base Terms. We credit that § 3.3 disapplies them where IBM is in breach and that § 4.2 late-payment fees are acceptable. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 14.10 Assignment | Sits at the fallback: assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition without consent; other assignments on consent not unreasonably withheld; no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for IBM. Noted: no express affiliate carve-out for us and no restriction on IBM's own assignment (IBM may subcontract under § 14.8). |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice (better than our preferred 30 days), IBM must perform through the final termination date, and IBM has no convenience right — only uncured material breach under § 3.3. The unquantified early termination charges are addressed under LD to avoid duplication. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or all-requirements obligation; charges apply to Services ordered under Order Forms and § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction. The § 14.11 bar on reselling the Services is a scope-of-use limit, not a restraint on our business lines. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal window | **Deviation** | § 3.2 Renewal | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our 60-day fallback, and renewal for a term "equal in duration to the previous term" produces automatic multi-year renewals on a multi-year Order Form — walk-away territory. Uncapped renewal pricing is mitigated by the § 13.1 fee-free exit and is noted only. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | IBM warrants only reasonable care and skill plus compliance with laws applicable to its own business. No conformance warranty for Materials or Base Components (supplied "AS IS"), no warranty period and no stated remedy; §§ 5.2/5.4 disclaim capacity, performance and secure operation. Fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund). |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations. Nothing requires IBM to provide transition assistance, return our Content in a usable format or delete it afterwards; the only return obligation runs against us (Materials, § 8.1). A material gap in a hosting agreement. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us and no access to our systems or premises. § 11.3 is an acceptable-use investigation right exercisable on reasonable-efforts prior notice. Matches our preferred position. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law is our preferred position; no arbitration or foreign venue. Noted: no express exclusive venue in New York County, and the § 14.14 two-year contractual limitations period is a separate point outside this rule. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No MFN or price-matching obligation on us. Pricing is set by Service Option Attachments and Order Forms; IBM price changes only after 12 months on 90 days' notice with a fee-free exit if we disagree (§ 13.1). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction in the Base Terms; charges apply to Services ordered and § 11.5 places capacity planning with us without committing volumes. To be re-confirmed against Attachment A and the Order Forms when provided. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction in § 14.8 or elsewhere. Matches our preferred position. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation anywhere in the Agreement; § 14.12 allocates risk of loss but requires no coverage. For a vendor hosting our environment and processing personal data on our behalf (§ 14.18), this is our walk-away case. |

## Walk-Away Items

The following three findings are identified in our review as walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Revocable, narrowly scoped Base Components licence (§ 12.1).** The licence is expressly revocable and runs to us alone, with no Affiliate or contractor coverage and no mechanism to add them. Our position: delete "revocable", tie termination of the licence to Section 3, and extend it to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.
2. **Automatic multi-year renewal (§ 3.2).** Renewal for a term "equal in duration to the previous term" on a 90-day non-renewal window rolls a multi-year Order Form into a further multi-year commitment. Our position: fix renewals at 12 months and shorten the notice window to 30 days.
3. **No vendor insurance covenant (§ 14.12 / Agreement-wide).** For a hosted environment and personal data processed on our behalf, the absence of any coverage requirement is unacceptable. Our position: insert a short insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' compensation) with certificates on request.

We would also treat the § 9.1 liability position as effectively non-negotiable in substance: the blanket exclusion of liability for loss of or damage to our records or data cannot stand in a hosting deal, and confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud must sit outside the cap alongside the indemnities.

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redlines.** Six drafting changes to go back to IBM:
   - § 9.1 — add a mutual carve-out sentence (confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud) and delete the exclusion of liability for loss of Customer data; confirm indemnities and confidentiality sit outside the cap.
   - § 12.1 — remove at-will revocability, tie licence termination to Section 3, and extend the licence to Affiliates and contractors.
   - § 3.2 — fix the renewal term at 12 months and the non-renewal notice window at 30 days.
   - § 3.4 — cap early termination charges at three months' charges for the terminated Services, as the sole amount payable on termination.
   - § 5.1 — add a 90-day conformance warranty for Materials and Base Components with a re-performance/repair/refund remedy, carved out of the §§ 5.2/5.4 disclaimers.
   - § 3.5 — insert transition assistance, return of Content within 30 days and certified deletion (§ 3.5 already survives termination under § 14.2); and insert the insurance covenant in the general terms.
2. **Obtain and review Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and the Order Forms.** These drive the early termination charges, the renewal term length, pricing and any minimum commitment. Our MINCOMMIT and LD conclusions are subject to that review.
3. **Table the secondary asks** as a single consolidated list to be traded rather than pressed individually: indemnity coverage for IBM's breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; narrowing our § 8.2(a)(3) reverse indemnity; broadening the Type II Materials licence (Enterprise scope, modify/sublicense) and tightening the Type I licence-back and default classification; an affirmative statement that we retain ownership of Content; an affiliate carve-out and a restriction on IBM's assignment; exclusive venue in New York County; and the § 14.14 two-year limitations period.
4. **Confirm the commercial appetite** on the three walk-away items with the business owner before the next call, so we can signal clearly which points are conditions of signature.

*This memo reflects only the findings supplied in this review and the sections cited above.*"}
